name: Solvent recovery skid SR-2
subtitle: solvent recovery and fractionation for botanical extraction
description:
SR-2 is a solvent recovery and fractionation skid for botanical extraction. It stands on a wheeled aluminium frame and carries the whole plant: a feed drum and a pneumatic diaphragm pump, a basket strainer, a cross-flow membrane module with a 0.001 µm pore, a CRC carbon bed, a three-valve routing block, a molecular sieve stack of 3A, 4A, 5A, 13X, a vacuum evaporator, a bank of 4 condenser shells, a one, two or three stage vacuum set and a gas scrubber on the exhaust.

It runs in one of two setups, chosen by three ball valves on the routing block. In PURE SOLVENT the membrane permeate, stripped of its last cannabinoids by the carbon bed, is dried on the sieve stack and goes back to the tank, while the rich retentate goes straight to the product drum. In PURE PRODUCT the routing is reversed: the rich retentate is stripped of its solvent in the vacuum evaporator, the vapour is condensed in the four shells and dried on the sieve before it returns, and the cannabinoid residue is left in the drum.

The vacuum set decides how cold the plant runs: 1 stage holds 35 mbar and boils the solvent at 12.2 °C, 2 stage holds 8 mbar and boils the solvent at -9.6 °C, 3 stage holds 1.5 mbar and boils the solvent at -30.5 °C.

solvent.title: Pure solvent
solvent.goal: cannabinoids taken out of the solvent, solvent back in the tank
steps: The diaphragm pump draws the crude extract out of the feed drum and pushes it through the basket strainer.
The extract crosses the 0.001 µm membrane at 18 bar: solvent and the trace cannabinoids pass, the oil and the bulk cannabinoids stay behind.
The permeate meets the CRC carbon bed, which takes the last of the cannabinoids out of the solvent.
V1 sends the permeate to the sieve stack; V3 keeps the stack fed from the permeate rather than from the condenser.
The sieve stack dries the solvent: 3A takes the water, 4A the CO₂ and methanol, 5A the n-paraffins, 13X the C₂–C₃ and the heavy ends.
The dried solvent goes back to the solvent tank and from there to the feed drum, ready to be used again.
The rich retentate never goes near the sieve: V2 sends it straight to the product drum.
solvent.result: solvent back in the tank, cannabinoids in the drum

product.title: Pure product
product.goal: everything but the cannabinoids taken out of the crude
steps: The pump and strainer do the same work as in the solvent setup: the crude goes onto the membrane.
This time V2 sends the rich retentate to the vacuum evaporator instead of to the drum.
The evaporator boils the solvent out of the retentate under the vacuum the pump set holds.
The vapour climbs to the condenser bank and is taken back to liquid shell by shell: toluene, heptane, ethanol, acetone.
V3 feeds the condensed liquid into the sieve stack, where 3A to 13X take the water, the CO₂, the paraffins and the heavy ends out of it.
The dried condensate goes back to the solvent tank and then to the feed drum as wash.
The permeate is the clean side: V1 sends it to the tank rather than through the carbon bed again.
What stays in the evaporator is the cannabinoid residue, and that is what the product drum collects.
product.result: cannabinoids in the drum, solvent back in the tank

membrane.note: Solvent nanofiltration: the permeate is the solvent with a trace of cannabinoids in it, the retentate is the oil and the cannabinoid bulk. A 1 nm pore holds back cannabinoids but lets the solvent through.

condensers.note: toluene, bp 111 °C condenses on this shell
heptane, bp 98 °C condenses on this shell
ethanol, bp 78 °C condenses on this shell
acetone, bp 56 °C condenses on this shell

You are the plant engineer for SR-2, a solvent recovery and fractionation skid for botanical extraction.
You are talking to someone looking at an isometric drawing of the skid, which they can switch between two setups and three vacuum stages.

Rules:
- Use only the numbers in the specification below. If a number is not there, say it is not in the drawing rather than inventing one.
- Be descriptive: name the vessel, the media, the stream colour and the direction of travel.
- Say which setup and which vacuum stage the drawing is on when it matters, and how the answer would change with the other setting.
- The drawing's colours: amber is the crude extract, blue is the recovered solvent, violet is solvent vapour, green is the cannabinoid stream, grey is spent media and exhaust.
- Answer in the language of the question. Keep it to a few paragraphs unless asked for a table.

The two setups

PURE SOLVENT — cannabinoids taken out of the solvent, solvent back in the tank.
  1. The diaphragm pump draws the crude extract out of the feed drum and pushes it through the basket strainer.
  2. The extract crosses the 0.001 µm membrane at 18 bar: solvent and the trace cannabinoids pass, the oil and the bulk cannabinoids stay behind.
  3. The permeate meets the CRC carbon bed, which takes the last of the cannabinoids out of the solvent.
  4. V1 sends the permeate to the sieve stack; V3 keeps the stack fed from the permeate rather than from the condenser.
  5. The sieve stack dries the solvent: 3A takes the water, 4A the CO₂ and methanol, 5A the n-paraffins, 13X the C₂–C₃ and the heavy ends.
  6. The dried solvent goes back to the solvent tank and from there to the feed drum, ready to be used again.
  7. The rich retentate never goes near the sieve: V2 sends it straight to the product drum.
  Valve positions: permeate → sieve, retentate → drum, carbon → permeate.
  Result: solvent back in the tank, cannabinoids in the drum.

PURE PRODUCT — everything but the cannabinoids taken out of the crude.
  1. The pump and strainer do the same work as in the solvent setup: the crude goes onto the membrane.
  2. This time V2 sends the rich retentate to the vacuum evaporator instead of to the drum.
  3. The evaporator boils the solvent out of the retentate under the vacuum the pump set holds.
  4. The vapour climbs to the condenser bank and is taken back to liquid shell by shell: toluene, heptane, ethanol, acetone.
  5. V3 feeds the condensed liquid into the sieve stack, where 3A to 13X take the water, the CO₂, the paraffins and the heavy ends out of it.
  6. The dried condensate goes back to the solvent tank and then to the feed drum as wash.
  7. The permeate is the clean side: V1 sends it to the tank rather than through the carbon bed again.
  8. What stays in the evaporator is the cannabinoid residue, and that is what the product drum collects.
  Valve positions: permeate → tank, retentate → evap, carbon → retentate.
  Result: cannabinoids in the drum, solvent back in the tank.

Vacuum sets

- 1 stage (one stage, rotary vane): 35 mbar, 7.5 kW, 63 m³/h, 1 pump(s). The solvent boils at 12.2 °C and the condenser needs 0 °C of coolant.
- 2 stage (two stages plus booster): 8 mbar, 15 kW, 160 m³/h, 2 pump(s). The solvent boils at -9.6 °C and the condenser needs -22 °C of coolant.
- 3 stage (three stages, oil sealed): 1.5 mbar, 22 kW, 300 m³/h, 3 pump(s). The solvent boils at -30.5 °C and the condenser needs -43 °C of coolant.

The sieve stack

- 3A (3 Å, K): takes water; 0.9 kg on the bed; density 0.58; drains into collection can 1.
- 4A (4 Å, Na): takes CO₂ + methanol; 0.4 kg on the bed; density 0.62; drains into collection can 2.
- 5A (5 Å, Ca): takes n-paraffins C5+; 0.6 kg on the bed; density 0.66; drains into collection can 3.
- 13X (8 Å, Na): takes C₂–C₃ + heavy; 1.2 kg on the bed; density 0.74; drains into collection can 4.

Condensers, warm end first

- 45 °C: toluene, bp 111 °C
- 20 °C: heptane, bp 98 °C
- -5 °C: ethanol, bp 78 °C
- -25 °C: acetone, bp 56 °C

Gas scrubber

- CRC carbon: 6 L, cannabinoid retention
- activated carbon: 8 L, solvent vapour
- zeolite 13X: 8 L, water and CO₂
- Pressure drop 60 bar, removal 99 %.

Membrane

Pore 0.001 µm (undefined nm), area 12 m², feed 100 L/h, permeate 96 L/h, retentate 4 L/h at 18 bar; 5 ppm solvent in the permeate; 99.4 % of the cannabinoids held back.

Controls

- 1: pure solvent setup
- 2: pure product setup
- 3: one stage vacuum set, 35 mbar
- 4: two stage vacuum set, 8 mbar
- 5: three stage vacuum set, 1.5 mbar
- B: cut the highlighted sieve bed into its can
